title: The +1 table
prompt: In the (m+1) x (n+1) LCS table, why does comparing `dp[i][j]` use `s1.charAt(i - 1)`?
options: dp[i][j] covers the first i characters — a prefix of LENGTH i — whose last character sits at index i-1
It's a bug that happens to work
explanation: Row/column 0 represent EMPTY prefixes so bases need no special-casing; the price is the persistent i-1/j-1 shift when touching the actual strings.

title: Drill: grid path count
prompt: From memory: count paths from the top-left to bottom-right of an m x n grid moving only right or down — but build the dp table yourself: `dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]`, first row and column all 1.

solution.explanation: Every cell is reached from above or from the left, so the counts add. Edge cells have exactly one approach — the base cases.

hints: Fill the first row and first column with 1 before the double loop.

title: Drill: minimum path sum
prompt: From memory (grid dp): moving only right or down from the top-left, return the minimum sum of values along a path to the bottom-right of `grid`.
hints: Fill the first row/column as running sums.
dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(from above, from left).
